result.topic_en: Euler finishes the sign rules for the second part of a general expression built from products and combinations of the sums ∫1/z^n and ∫1/z^m (written as series in n and m). He then begins showing how these expressions shorten when m and n are even or odd.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 149
vbi ſigna ſuperiora valent, ſi $m$ ſit numerus par; inferiora vero ſi $m$ ſit numerus impar.
Pars altera.
$+(1\pm 1)\int\frac{1}{z^n}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^m}\mp\int\frac{1}{z^n}\left(\frac{1}{y^m}\right)$
$-\frac{n}{1}(1\mp 1)\int\frac{1}{z^{n+1}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{m-1}}\pm\frac{n}{1}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+1}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{m-1}}\right)$
$+\frac{n(n+1)}{1.\,2}(1\pm 1)\int\frac{1}{z^{n+2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{m-2}}\mp\frac{n(n+1)}{1.\,2.}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+2}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{m-2}}\right)$
$-\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.\,2.\,3}(1\mp 1)\int\frac{1}{z^{n+3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{m-3}}\pm\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.\,2.\,3}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+3}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{m-3}}\right)$
etc.
vbi ſigna ſuperiora valent, ſi $n$ numerus par, contra vero valent inferiora.
8. Prout ergo exponentes $m$ et $n$ fuerint vel pares vel impares, hae expreſſiones ad pauciores terminos reducuntur, erit ſcilicet
Pars prima ſi m ſit numerus par.
$+2\int\frac{1}{z^m}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^n}-\int\frac{1}{z^m}\left(\frac{1}{y^n}\right)-\frac{m}{1}\int\frac{1}{z^{m+1}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{n-1}}\right)$
$+\frac{2m(m+1)}{1.\,2.}\int\frac{1}{z^{m+2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{n-2}}-\frac{m(m+1)}{1.\,2}\int\frac{1}{z^{m+2}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{n-2}}\right)$
$-\frac{(m+1)(m+2)}{1.\,2.\,3}\int\frac{1}{z^{m+3}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{n-3}}\right)$ [?]
etc.
T 3 ſiue

items.quote: Prout ergo exponentes $m$ et $n$ fuerint vel pares vel impares, hae expreſſiones ad pauciores terminos reducuntur
items.english: Therefore, according as the exponents m and n are either even or odd, these expressions are reduced to fewer terms.
